title: Music shows an instructor's whole library song list, and library search reaches all of it
acceptance: Liked or library songs are not cut off at 200 for Apple Music, Spotify or SoundCloud: the list pages (a "Load more" or incremental load), or loads the full set within a documented upper bound that says when it is reached.
Search on the Songs list finds a song that sits past the first page, either by loading it or by a server-side search.
"Create class from liked songs" uses the same paging and says when it used a subset.
The "Recents" sort is relabeled or reimplemented: today it is the provider's own order (alphabetical for Apple library songs), not recency.
GET /providers/:provider/likes changes are registered in generate-openapi.ts and the OpenAPI drift and contract-parity checks pass; the iOS snapshot refresh is a separate iOS PR.
No provider audio or derived data is cached; any paging cursor is the provider's own.

filterLibrary filters only the loaded rows; orderLibrary returns provider order for "recents". Checked on main c9b89a7.

resolution: Met for Apple Music and SoundCloud under the owner's 2026-10-29 narrowing. GET /providers/:provider/likes returns about 200 songs per page (whole provider pages) and the opaque next cursor (the provider's own continuation, provider-bound, never stored) in X-RitmoFit-Next-Cursor; the body stays a bare TrackSearchResult[]. Music › Songs has Load more. Songs search reaches past the first page: Apple Music searches the library server-side (?q=, Apple library search); SoundCloud and Spotify keep loading pages while a query is typed up to 1,000 songs, then say "Searched your first 1,000 liked songs" and offer Keep loading. Create class from liked songs uses the same loaded pages and says when it used a subset. "Recents" is relabeled "Library order" on Playlists and Songs (no provider exposes a recency sort for these lists). OpenAPI registers cursor, q, the header and 422; drift and contract-parity pass. Nothing provider-derived is cached. Spotify paging ships mock-tested only; its live check is RF-148 (dependsOn RF-92). TrackSearch likes mode still reads the first page: RF-149. Real Apple and SoundCloud paging on the owner's accounts is a post-deploy check named in the PR; the iOS OpenAPI snapshot refresh is a separate iOS PR.
